b2-33-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Freedom Is
b2-33-01.scenario: In the cold library room in Budapest, the thinker asks you what freedom is and which guarantee is missing from public life.
b2-33-01.prompt: Tell him what freedom is and which guarantee is missing.
b2-33-01.target: A szabadság az nem más, mint a személyes felelősség vállalása. Éppen az a garancia hiányzik, ami a hatalom korlátozásához szükséges.
b2-33-01.english: Freedom is none other than taking personal responsibility. Precisely that guarantee is missing which is necessary to limit power.
b2-33-01.canDo: I can construct emphatic cleft identification sentences using the formula az nem más, mint ...

b2-33-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why the Talks Stalled
b2-33-02.scenario: In the library room, the thinker asks you why the talks between the two sides stalled.
b2-33-02.prompt: Tell him why the talks stalled, and link the cause to the result with a formal phrase.
cues: Say what was missing between the sides
Say what happened to the talks
b2-33-02.target: Abból adódóan, hogy hiányzott a bizalom, a tárgyalások megfeneklettek.
b2-33-02.english: Because trust was missing, the talks stalled.
b2-33-02.canDo: I can express sophisticated causal deductions using abból adódóan, hogy ...

b2-33-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Fear Does
b2-33-03.scenario: The thinker asks you what fear does to a nation that lives in it for a long time.
b2-33-03.prompt: Tell him what fear does to the nation, and what hysteria does to its politics.
cues: Say what fear does to the nation's sense of reality
Say what political hysteria does to compromise
b2-33-03.target: A félelem eltorzítja a nemzet valóságérzékét. A politikai hisztéria megbénítja a józan kompromisszumkeresést.
b2-33-03.english: Fear distorts the nation's sense of reality. Political hysteria paralyses sober compromise-seeking.
b2-33-03.canDo: I can explain political hysteria with the lesson's key words, such as valóságérzék and téveszme

b2-33-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Must Answer
b2-33-04.scenario: The thinker asks you what the rule of law is and what protects citizens from those who hold power.
b2-33-04.prompt: Tell him what the rule of law is and what protects the citizens.
cues: Define the rule of law in one sentence
Say what leaders owe the citizens
b2-33-04.target: A jogállamiság az nem más, mint a törvény előtti egyenlőség garanciája. A vezetők nyilvános elszámoltathatósága védi meg a polgárokat.
b2-33-04.english: The rule of law is none other than the guarantee of equality before the law. The public accountability of leaders protects the citizens.
b2-33-04.canDo: I can define the rule of law with az nem más, mint ...

b2-33-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Opening an Essay
b2-33-05.scenario: The thinker asks how you will begin your essay on freedom and fear, and what makes your reasoning strong.
b2-33-05.prompt: Tell him how you will begin and what the strength of your reasoning comes from.
cues: Say what the strength of the reasoning comes from
b2-33-05.target: Mindenekelőtt alapos fogalmi tisztázással kezdek. Az érvelés ereje abból adódik, hogy a következtetés levezethető az előfeltevésekből.
b2-33-05.english: First of all I begin with a thorough clarification of concepts. The strength of the reasoning comes from the fact that the conclusion can be derived from the premises.
b2-33-05.canDo: I can open an essay with a conceptual clarification (fogalmi tisztázás)

b2-33-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Freedom and Its Danger
b2-33-consolidation.scenario: Before you leave the library room, the thinker asks for your view of what protects freedom and where the trouble came from.
b2-33-consolidation.prompt: Give him your view in two sentences: what protects freedom, and where the trouble came from.
cues: Say where the trouble came from
b2-33-consolidation.target: A jogállamiság az nem más, mint a hatalom korlátozása. A baj abból adódott, hogy a polgárok a bűnbakképzést választották.
b2-33-consolidation.english: The rule of law is none other than the limiting of power. The trouble arose from the fact that citizens chose scapegoating.
b2-33-consolidation.canDo: I can define a political idea with az nem más, mint ... and éppen az, ami ...
